questions.q: A magnetic needle free to rotate in a vertical plane parallel to the magnetic meridian has its north tip pointing down at ${22}^{0}$ with the horizontal. The horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field at the place is known to be $\text{0}\text{.35 G}$. questions.solution:
Given, angle of dip $\delta = 2 {2}^{o}$

Horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field $\text{H = 0}\text{.35 G}$

Let the magnitude of the earth's magnetic field at the place is $\text{R}$.

Using the formula, $H = \text{R} \text\cos \delta$

or $\text{R} = \dfrac{\text{H}}{\text\cos \delta} = \dfrac{0 \text{.} 3 5}{\text\cos 2 {2}^{o}} = \dfrac{0 \text{.} 3 5}{0 \text{.} 9 2 7 2} = 0 \text{.} 3 8 \text{G}$

{\theta_{{1}}$ = 90 °${\theta_{{2}}$ = 0 °$

{\theta_{{1}}$ = 0 °${\theta_{{2}}$ = - 90 °$

${W}_{2} = MB $\left(cos ⁡ 0 ° - cos ⁡ \left(- 90 °\right)\right)$

Total workdone

Magnetic field $= {B}_{H}$

$T = \dfrac{60}{12} = 5sec.$

Magnetic field $= {B}_{H} + B$

$T = \dfrac{60}{15} = 4sec.$

Let after reversing magnetic needle makes $x$ oscillation per minute.

$⇒$ Magnetic field $= {B}_{H} - B, T = \dfrac{60}{x}sec.$

$T ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{Magneticfield}} ⇒ \dfrac{5}{4} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{B}_{H} + B}{{B}_{H}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B}{{B}_{H}} = \dfrac{9}{16}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{\left(\dfrac{60}{x}\right)} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{B}_{H} - B}{{B}_{H}}}$

$⇒x = \sqrt{63}$

$= \dfrac{1 {0}^{- 7} \times 2 \times 0 \text{.} 4 8}{{\left(0 \text{.} 1\right)}^{3}} = 0 \text{.} 9 6 \times 1 {0}^{- 4} \text{T}$

The direction of the magnetic field is along the direction of the magnetic moment. We know that the direction of magnetic moment is from S to N pole. Thus, the direction of the magnetic field is from S to N pole of the magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the magnetic dipole moment of an atom of diamagnetic material, paramagnetic material and ferromagnetic material is denoted by ${\mu}_{d}, {\mu}_{p}$ and ${\mu}_{f}$ respectively, then
questions.solution:
The magnetic dipole moment of a diamagnetic material is zero as each of its pair of electrons has opposite spins, i.e., ${\mu}_{d} = 0.$ Paramagnetic substances have dipole moment > 0, i.e., ${\mu}_{p} \ne 0$, because of the excess of electrons in its molecules spinning in the same direction.

Ferromagnetic substances are very strong magnets and they also have a permanent magnetic moment, i.e., ${\mu}_{f} \ne 0.$

options:
$4. 8 \times {10}^{- 2}J$
&
questions.solution:
For the unstable equilibrium, the angle between the magnetic moment and magnetic field is 180^{o}. ( $∵$ In this position it will be in a direction to magnetic field thus no torque will act on it.)

$\theta = 1 8 {0}^{o}$

The potential energy of the magnet

& $U = - mBcos{180}^{°}$

& & & & $= - 0. 32 \times 0. 15 ( - 1 ) = 4. 8 \times {10}^{- 2}J$

Thus, for the unstable equilibrium, the potential energy is $4. 8 \times {10}^{- 2}J$.
